key_insight: eMOOD replaces MOOD's classical troubled-cell test with entropy production, enabling more targeted shock detection in high-order finite-volume solvers.
engineering_relevance: The method improves robustness and scalability for unstructured-mesh compressible-flow simulations by reducing unnecessary cell flagging, memory traffic, and runtime.
method: Uses numerical entropy generation as a compact-stencil troubled-cell indicator.
Integrates the detector into both a classical MOOD cascade and a MOOD-CWENO hybrid.
Activates nonlinear reconstruction only where entropy signals non-smooth flow.
evidence_signal: Across shock and multiphase benchmarks, eMOOD flagged up to 75% fewer cells and delivered speed-ups of up to 20% while maintaining solution quality.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on how well entropy production isolates true flow discontinuities, so detector tuning and robustness on different mesh/physics regimes remain important.
paper_title: eMOOD: Entropy-Based Multidimensional Optimal Order Detection for High-Order Shock-Capturing Finite-Volume Schemes
